newsitem.title: FRANCE: CCF rises on expected ratings upgrade.
newsitem.headline: CCF rises on expected ratings upgrade.

text.p: Shares in French bank Credit Commercial de France traded higher following comments from its chairman Charles de Croisset that he expected an upgrade in its debt rating.

Traders said they were surprised that a company chairman should announce that a ratings upgrade was due. "It's a bit surprising. But credit has to be given that CCF is doing pretty well and is one of the rare French banks that can be a upgraded," said one operator.
CCF shares were up two francs at 234, or 0.86 percent, at 1241 GMT. It had been down 0.12 percent before the comment.
De Croisset said at a business conference earlier that the bank was very solid and that its rating was in the process of being raised.
